correctness.rationale: For each initial tree distance up to four, first-round eligibility is exhausted by unique-tree-geodesic constraints, yielding w1=1, w2=2p-p², w3=2p²-p³, w4=p³ and zero further. An explicit same-order common-coin coupling isolates a four-coin absence event of probability (1-p)^4; conditional on it the additional central branch gives a witness at round three with probability (2p-p²)p², hence p^4(2-p)(1-p)^4. Finite-state integer-polynomial checker independently validates all stated path identities; 1,356 all-tree pair checks for sizes 2..5 match the kernel. The ER mean-degree limit uses an established fixed-round local-convergence theorem, the PGW(c) local weak limit, and uniform fixed-radius degree moments.

value.rationale: Repeated closure is motivated as a mechanism for graph clustering not captured by one round. The exact all-tree distance-only two-round kernel and sparse random-graph degree polynomial make the repeated process quantitatively tractable; the exact positive same-order branching defect identifies the earliest round and smallest graph order at which a radial approximation ceases to be exact. It is a structural boundary, not a mechanical restatement of published local convergence.
